Shall the City Charter be amended to increase the minimum budget allocated to the Department of Recreation and Parks, phased in over ten years until it is double the current minimum budget allocation, with exceptions for fiscal emergencies? Supporters: LA City Councilmembers, Monica Rodriguez, Imelda Padilla & Ysabel Jurado; LA City Controller, Kenneth Mejia; Father Greg Boyle Opponents: None submitted.

Title: LOS ANGELES CITY GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION - MEASURE PRT
MeasureText: CITY AIRPORTS, HARBOR, AND WATER AND POWER DEPARTMENTS. CHARTER AMENDMENT PRT. Shall the City Charter be amended to: require the Harbor Department to allocate funds for waterfront public access projects; require disclosure of workforce impacts for certain Harbor Department leases and agreements; increase maximum terms for certain leases; and change the composition requirement for the Airport Commission? Supporters: Tim McOsker, LA City Councilmember; Imelda Padilla, LA City Councilwoman; Traci Park, LA City Councilwoman Opponents: None submitted.

Title: LOS ANGELES CITY GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION - MEASURE SC
MeasureText: CAMPAIGN FINANCE RULES RELATED TO BOARD OF EDUCATION ELECTIONS. CHARTER AMENDMENT SC. Shall the Los Angeles City Charter be amended to clarify the campaign finance rules for Board of Education elections and allow for changes by ordinance? Supporters: Councilmember, Adrin Nazarian; LAUSD Board Member, Nick Melvoin; League of Women Voters of Greater LA; CA Common Cause Opponents: None submitted.

Title: LOS ANGELES CITY GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION - MEASURE TE
MeasureText: PROPERTY TRANSFER TAX EXEMPTION FOR VICTIMS OF JANUARY 2025 FIRE DISASTER. PROPOSITION TE. Shall an ordinance be adopted to provide a one-time exemption from the City's special documentary transfer tax (Proposition ULA) for residential properties that were damaged or destroyed in the Palisades Fire and are sold within five years of the date of the Fire? Supporters: Councilmember Park; Mayor Bass; Council President Harris-Dawson; Western States Carpenters; Palisades Community Council Opponents: None submitted.

Title: BELLFLOWER UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT SPECIAL ELECTION - MEASURE SM
MeasureText: With funds that cannot be taken by the State and spent elsewhere, shall Bellflower Unified School District's measure to repair/replace deteriorating roofs, plumbing, heating, ventilation and electrical systems; upgrade classrooms, labs and career training facilities; and, improve access for students with disabilities be adopted, authorizing $135 million in bonds levying $49 per $100,000 assessed value ($8 million annually) while outstanding, with legal rates, audits, citizen oversight, no funds for administrator salaries and full disclosure of all spending? Supporters: Asm. José Solache; Sup. Janice Hahn; Dr. Robinson, BUSD Teacher; John Young, BTA Pres.; Mayra Garza, BUSD School Board Pres. Opponents: None submitted.

Title: CHARTER OAK UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT SPECIAL ELECTION - MEASURE S
MeasureText: To provide safe, modern neighborhood schools by repairing/upgrading/equipping aging classrooms, science labs, instructional technology, and school facilities that support math, science, engineering, literacy, arts, skilled trades, and college/career readiness, fixing deteriorating roofs, plumbing, electrical systems, and removing asbestos/lead pipes, shall Charter Oak Unified School District's measure authorizing $75,000,000 in bonds at legal rates be adopted, levying $40 per $100,000 assessed value ($5,000,000 annually) while bonds are outstanding, with independent oversight/audits, all money locally controlled? Supporters: Charter Oak PTA Council; Covina Police Officers Assn.; Charter Oak Education Foundation; Cristian Aguilar, COUSD Board Pres. Opponents: None submitted.

Title: CLAREMONT UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT SPECIAL ELECTION - MEASURE CS
MeasureText: CLAREMONT UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT CLASSROOM SAFETY, HEALTH AND REPAIR MEASURE. To repair/upgrade aging classrooms, heating/air conditioning/electrical/plumbing systems, improve safety/security, fix leaky/deteriorating roofs, repair/construct/equip classroom sites/facilities without increasing current taxes, shall the Claremont Unified School District's measure authorizing $77,000,000 of bonds at legal rates, levying approximately $32/$100,000 of assessed value ($5,000,000 annually) while bonds are outstanding, be adopted, requiring audits/independent oversight, no money for inappropriate administrator salaries, all funds staying local? Supporters: John Faranda; Sue Keith; John Neiuber; Brett O'Connor; Phalana Tiller Opponents: James M. Belna; Donna Lowe; Gary Lowe; Joyce H. Sauter; Deborah Barker-Benfield

Title: EL RANCHO UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT SPECIAL ELECTION - MEASURE ED
MeasureText: With funds that cannot be taken by the State or Federal government, shall El Rancho Unified School District's measure to update inefficient heating and air-conditioning systems; replace aging plumbing and roofs; improve school safety; and modernize and equip classrooms and facilities be adopted, authorizing $118 million in bonds with legal rates, average annual levies below $55 per $100,000 of assessed valuation ($7.9 million annually while outstanding), annual audits, no administrator salaries, independent oversight, and disclosure of all spending? Supporters: Bob Archuleta; Marco Zapian; Paul Camacho; Guadalupe Diaz; Raul Leos Sr. Opponents: None submitted.

Title: GLENDORA UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT SPECIAL ELECTION - MEASURE G
MeasureText: Glendora Unified School District Classroom Repair Extension Measure. To repair or replace deteriorating roofs, plumbing, HVAC, electrical systems; remove asbestos and lead pipes; upgrade classrooms, labs, facilities to support college/career readiness in math, science, engineering, technology and skilled trades; shall Glendora Unified School District's measure be adopted, authorizing $86,000,000 in bonds at legal rates (without increasing current tax rates), levying approximately $33 per $100,000 assessed value ($5,000,000 annually) while bonds are outstanding, with independent oversight/audits, and funds locally controlled? Supporters: Art Ludwick; Glendora Ed Foundation; Dr. Cliff Hamlow, Fmr Mayor, Glendora Teachers Assoc.; Mendell Thompson, City Council Opponents: Mel Bennett

Title: HACIENDA LA PUENTE UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT SPECIAL ELECTION - MEASURE B
MeasureText: Shall members of the Board of Education of the Hacienda La Puente Unified School District be limited to serving no more than two (2) four-year terms during their lifetime regardless of the trustee area represented? Supporters: None submitted Opponents: None submitted.

Title: HAWTHORNE SCHOOL DISTRICT SPECIAL ELECTION - MEASURE HH
MeasureText: HAWTHORNE SCHOOL DISTRICT SCHOOL REPAIR/IMPROVEMENT MEASURE. To repair aging classrooms, ensure student health, safety and achievement and update technology, upgrade aging plumbing, electrical, lighting, heating/ventilation, safety/security systems, shall this Hawthorne School District measure be adopted to repair, construct, acquire classrooms, facilities, sites/equipment, and issue $110,000,000 in bonds, at legal rates, levy on average $30 per $100,000 assessed value (averaging $5,240,000 annually) while bonds are outstanding, require independent audits/oversight, all money for local schools? Supporters: HSD Board of Trustees; Cristina Chiappe; Sergio R. Mortara; Vicente Bravo; Luciano A. Aguilar; Dr. Eugene M. Krank Opponents: None submitted.

Title: INGLEWOOD UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT SPECIAL ELECTION - MEASURE MM
MeasureText: Inglewood Unified School District Safety, Repair, Upgrade Measure. To repair/upgrade classrooms/labs including science, engineering, career/skilled trades to help recruit/retain teachers; repair deteriorating gas lines; remove asbestos, lead paint, mold; provide safe drinking water; construct, repair equip sites, facilities; shall Inglewood Unified School District's measure authorizing $396,000,000 in bonds, at legal rates, levying $60 per $100,000 of assessed valuation ($26,000,000 annually) while bonds are outstanding, be adopted, requiring oversight, audits, spending disclosure, all funds for local schools? Supporters: Small Businessowner Moody; YMCA of Metro LA; Civic Leader Marcie Brown; Building Trades E. Medrano; Board Pres. Dr. McGhee Opponents: None submitted.

Title: KEPPEL UNION SCHOOL DISTRICT SPECIAL ELECTION - MEASURE K
MeasureText: Keppel Union School District Classroom Repair, Safety, Upgrade Measure. To repair leaky roofs, deteriorating plumbing, electrical, gas lines; provide safe drinking water; remove asbestos, lead paint, mold; improve fire safety, security, emergency communications; ensure safe children's play areas; upgrade classroom technology, science labs; shall Keppel Union School District's measure authorizing $27,000,000 in bonds at legal rates, levies averaging $30 per $100,000 assessed valuation ($1,700,000 annually) while bonds are outstanding, be adopted, requiring oversight, audits, spending disclosure, all funds for local schools? Supporters: Fmr Trustee Dominique Ballante; LocalBiz MonrealAuto; Deputy Sheriff Cronin; LocalBiz QuePaisa; Fmr Trustee Matthew Gaines Opponents: None submitted.

Title: LAS VIRGENES UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT SPECIAL ELECTION - MEASURE LV
AdditionalText: Los Angeles County Results Only (Shared with Ventura County)
MeasureText: To protect the quality of education in local schools and continue funding for math, science, technology, engineering, arts, skilled trades, and advanced programs that prepare students for success in college/careers; attracting and retaining highly qualified teachers; and maintaining manageable class sizes, shall Las Virgenes Unified School District's measure renewing the existing school parcel tax at the current $98 rate (no increase) for twelve years be adopted, with senior exemptions and all funds ($2,000,000 annually) benefiting local students? Supporters: Richard Sherman, CPHOA Pres.; Karen Zak Kent, DDS; Dr. Kirk Tamaddon, LVUSD Oversight Comm.; Joe Seetoo, CFA; Angie Falk Opponents: None submitted.

Title: PASADENA AREA COMMUNITY COLLEGE DISTRICT SPECIAL ELECTION - MEASURE UP
MeasureText: PASADENA CITY COLLEGE MEASURE PRESERVING AFFORDABLE HIGHER EDUCATION/CAREER TRAINING WITHOUT INCREASING TAX RATES. To construct/equip classrooms/career training facilities to prepare students for careers in nursing/healthcare, firefighting/EMS, construction, hospitality, and skilled trades; fix deteriorating roofs, plumbing/electrical systems, shall Pasadena Area Community College District's measure be adopted authorizing $485,000,000 in bonds at legal rates, without exceeding the current $9 per $100,000 assessed value (no increase), providing $27,000,000 annually while bonds are outstanding, with independent oversight/local control? Supporters: US Sen Adam Schiff; US Rep Judy Chu; CA Asm John Harabedian; SGV Economic Partnership; Charmayne Mills-Ealy, PCC Foundation Opponents: None submitted.

Title: SAN MARINO UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT SPECIAL ELECTION - MEASURE SMS
MeasureText: San Marino Unified School District Quality Education Measure Without increasing the existing rates and to protect/maintain quality education programs, classroom instruction, prevent class size increases or teaching position reductions, attract/retain high-quality teachers/employees, support advanced programs in math, science, engineering, technology, shall San Marino Unified School District's measure to combine and renew their existing parcel taxes for 6 years at $1,499 (combined) with senior exemptions, raising approximately $6,100,000 annually, annual adjustments, requiring spending disclosure be adopted? Supporters: Mandy Saber, President, San Marino Council of PTAs; Karla Domier; Janice Lee; Paul Callahan; Dr. Peter Koh, OD Opponents: None submitted.

Title: TEMPLE CITY UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT SPECIAL ELECTION - MEASURE TCS
MeasureText: WITHOUT INCREASING EXISTING TAX RATES, to upgrade safety/security and HVAC systems; remove asbestos/lead pipes; repair/upgrade/equip aging classrooms, science labs, school/career technology facilities to support college/career readiness in math, science, technology, arts, medical science, skilled trades; shall Temple City Unified School District's measure be adopted authorizing $146,000,000 in bonds at legal rates, levying $43 per $100,000 assessed value (averaging $8,710,000 annually) while bonds are outstanding, with independent citizen oversight, audits, all money locally controlled? Supporters: William Man, TC Mayor; Ryan Liu, PCC Trustee; TC Schools Foundation; Jerry Jambazian; Tim Huang, Chinese Amer. Assn Pres. Opponents: None submitted.

Title: VALLE LINDO SCHOOL DISTRICT SPECIAL ELECTION - MEASURE R
MeasureText: To improve the quality of education; replace old heating, ventilation and air-conditioning systems; modernize outdated classrooms, restrooms and school facilities; and repair or replace leaky roofs; shall Valle Lindo School District's measure be adopted authorizing $9,200,000 of bonds at legal rates, generating on average $536,000 annually while bonds are outstanding at a rate of approximately $29 per $100,000 assessed value, with annual audits, independent citizens' oversight committee, NO money for salaries and no money taken by the State? Supporters: Veronica Lauria, Valle Lindo SD Board President; Roxanna Nava; Marissa Lopez Newton; Nydia Romero; Michael Thompson Opponents: None submitted.
